Build the NxCloud MVP for the Nxeon platform — a managed, per-customer Nextcloud (Dropbox-style file hosting) provisioned as a VM reusing the existing Proxmox VPS provisioner. Work EXCLUSIVELY in the git worktree at /opt/nxeon-wt-nxcloud (branch feature/nxcloud). Do not touch /opt/nxeon or other worktrees. node_modules is symlinked there.

FIRST: read the full spec at /tmp/claude-0/-root/4f329df3-66ee-49c8-a6c5-615ecf189efc/scratchpad/ideas/nxcloud-spec.md (Approach A: per-customer Nextcloud VM, ~95% reuse of the VPS provisioner in worker/index.ts PROVISION path, inheriting billing/renewal/portal). Build the MVP it defines.

RULES (critical):
- Do NOT run `npm run build`, `next build`, `prisma generate`, or `prisma db push`. Write code only — staging is the gate (orchestrator runs it).
- Reuse, don't reinvent: study worker/index.ts (PROVISION) + VM provisioning helpers, lib/order.ts (VPS order), lib/actions.ts, the Server model + dashboard/servers UI, and marketing product pages. NxCloud rides the same Proxmox provisioner + billing/renewal stack. Prefer modeling an NxCloud instance on the existing Server/plan machinery (or a thin new model reusing the provisioner) as the spec recommends — Nextcloud provides the app; do NOT build a file-sync engine.
- MONEY SAFETY: ordering matches the audited VPS flow (atomic wallet/card, displayed===charged, renewals bill full). Do NOT apply first-month-free to NxCloud (that promo is shared-hosting only). Reuse orderQuote/placeOrder patterns.
- Provisioning: add a cloud-init/install path that stands up Nextcloud on the VM (snap or docker per spec), idempotent, reusing the repo's serving verifier + COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES alerting.
- Scope to a shippable MVP: order → provision Nextcloud VM → customer sees the instance with URL + credentials + basic status in the portal, plus a marketing page. Flag anything deferred. Prioritize a correct, coherent end-to-end skeleton over breadth — this is the biggest task.

DELIVER end-to-end: schema (plan/instance model per spec), order flow, worker provisioning task, customer portal panel/tab, admin visibility, a plan seed, and an app/(marketing)/nxcloud marketing page in the design system. Then in the worktree:
1. `git add -A && git commit -m "feat: NxCloud MVP — managed per-customer Nextcloud VM"` ending with: Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
2. `git push -u origin feature/nxcloud`
REPORT (factual, detailed): files changed, exact schema additions, seed/setting needed, provisioning steps the worker runs, the money flow, how much reuses the VPS provisioner vs new code, and everything deferred. Don't claim tested.

1	# NxCloud — Product Feasibility Spec (idea stage)
2	
3	**A self-hostable Dropbox / Nextcloud-style file hosting & sync product for the Nxeon platform.**
4	
5	Status: research + feasibility, feeds a go/no-go decision. No code written.
6	Author: research agent · Date: 2026-08-11 · Repo read-only (`/opt/nxeon`)
7	
8	---
9	
10	## 0. TL;DR / Recommendation
11	
12	**Ship NxCloud as a managed, per-customer Nextcloud instance provisioned as a VM (Approach A).** It reuses the Proxmox VPS provisioner Nxeon already runs (`worker/index.ts` PROVISION path), inherits the whole billing/renewal/portal stack for free, and — crucially — gives every customer a **hard VM boundary** instead of the app-level tenant isolation that just bit us on shared hosting (`lib/actions-hosting.ts` `isHostnameClaimed`, the HIGH-1/HIGH-2 cross-tenant vhost bugs). Nextcloud delivers ~95% of the customer-facing feature set (web UI, desktop/mobile sync, share links, versioning) out of the box, so the build is a **thin provisioner + a customer panel tab**, not a file-sync engine.
13	
14	- **Do NOT build a custom sync service** (Approach C). Sync clients, conflict resolution, delta-transfer, and end-to-end encryption are years of work Nextcloud has already done. Zero differentiation for a VPS reseller.
15	- **Do NOT do shared multi-tenant Nextcloud** (Approach B) as the launch product. One Nextcloud, many customers = exactly the blast-radius we just spent an audit closing on shared hosting. Revisit only for a cheap "Starter" tier *after* the isolated product proves demand.
16	- **Fastest sellable MVP: ~1.5–2.5 focused engineering days** by cloning the shared-hosting product shape onto a "provision a Nextcloud AIO container/VM" job. Details in §8.
17	
18	**Go recommendation: YES, as a fast-follow VPS add-on.** Low incremental effort, high strategic fit (Nxeon = "central hub for all projects" per memory), and it directly counters Dropbox/pCloud with a privacy/sovereignty angle. The margin is thin per-instance (a Nextcloud VM costs the same to run as a small VPS), so price it as a *packaged convenience* over "just rent a VPS," not as a storage price war.
19	
20	---
21	
22	## 1. Approach options
23	
24	### Approach A — Managed per-customer Nextcloud instance (RECOMMENDED)
25	One Nextcloud stack per customer, isolated at the VM (or rootless-Docker-per-user) boundary, provisioned via the existing Proxmox pipeline. Official install path is **Nextcloud All-in-One (AIO)** — a single Docker mastercontainer that brings up the full stack (Apache, DB, Redis, Talk, Collabora, backups) and auto-fetches Let's Encrypt when you point a domain at it. A host reverse proxy (Caddy/nginx) can fan many instances behind one IP by hostname.
26	
27	| | |
28	|---|---|
29	| **Effort** | Low. Reuses PROVISION path; the "new" work is a cloud-init/AIO bootstrap script + a panel tab. |
30	| **Differentiation** | Medium. "Your own private cloud, we run it" — privacy/sovereignty vs Dropbox. Per-tenant custom domain, no per-user SaaS tax. |
31	| **Isolation/security** | **Strongest.** Kernel/VM boundary. A Nextcloud RCE or misconfig is contained to one customer — the shared-hosting cross-tenant class of bug (`isHostnameClaimed`, per-user FPM jails) simply cannot occur. |
32	| **Cost/margin** | Weakest of the three per-GB — each instance carries a full VM's RAM/CPU. Mitigate with AIO-in-container-per-user on a shared box for the cheap tier later. |
33	| **Ops** | Per-instance updates/patching. Nextcloud AIO has a built-in auto-updater + backup, which offloads most of this to the appliance. |
34	
35	### Approach B — Shared multi-tenant Nextcloud
36	One (or a few) big Nextcloud instances; each customer is a Nextcloud "user" or group, quota-limited. Cheapest per-GB.
37	
38	- **Effort:** Medium — needs a provisioner that creates *users inside* an instance via Nextcloud's OCS/provisioning API, quota management, and a capacity/sharding scheduler.
39	- **Differentiation:** Low. It's just cheaper storage.
40	- **Isolation/security: the dealbreaker.** This is structurally the same trust model as shared hosting: many untrusted tenants sharing one app, one DB, one filesystem. Nextcloud's per-user separation is app-level ACLs — one auth/ACL bug (they ship them) is a **cross-customer data breach**, and a resource-hog tenant degrades everyone. We *just* found HIGH-severity cross-tenant bugs in our own shared-hosting layer; taking on someone else's multi-tenant attack surface for the flagship tier is the wrong lesson to ignore.
41	- **Verdict:** Not the launch product. Viable *later* as a low-cost "Starter 25 GB" tier once we accept the blast radius knowingly and put it behind the same "inert until security-reviewed" flag discipline shared hosting uses (`ENABLE_SHARED_HOSTING`).
42	
43	### Approach C — Custom file-sync service
44	Build our own storage backend + sync protocol + clients.
45	
46	- **Effort:** Very high (multi-month). Delta sync, conflict resolution, chunked/resumable upload, client apps for 3 OSes + mobile, E2E crypto, sharing, previews, trash/versioning.
47	- **Differentiation:** Negative until parity — we'd ship a worse Dropbox for a year.
48	- **Verdict:** No. This is a company, not a feature. Reject.
49	
50	**Recommendation: A now, B as an optional cheap tier post-launch, C never.**
51	
52	---
53	
54	## 2. How NxCloud reuses existing Nxeon infrastructure
55	
56	NxCloud is deliberately shaped as **"a VPS that boots pre-configured as Nextcloud."** Almost everything already exists:
57	
58	| Nxeon subsystem | Reuse for NxCloud |
59	|---|---|
60	| **Provisioner** (`worker/index.ts` PROVISION, `lib/proxmox.ts`) | Clone the VM, resize disk to plan size (`effectiveDiskGB`), then run a bootstrap step that installs Docker + Nextcloud AIO. Same clone→resize→cloud-init pipeline as a VPS; add one "install app" phase (pattern already exists in `worker/apps.ts` / `lib/actions-hosting.ts` app-install tasks). |
61	| **Node scheduler** (`lib/order.ts` `scheduleNode`, capacity checks) | Identical least-loaded RAM placement. NxCloud plans are just VPS sizes with a storage bias. |
62	| **Order + billing core** (`lib/order.ts` `placeOrder`/`orderQuote`, wallet, invoices, coupons) | A near-clone of the VPS order flow (or literally a VPS plan with an `appTemplate=nextcloud` flag). Wallet debit, invoice line items, promo/coupon plumbing, `OrderPrice` sold-price carry — all reused verbatim. This is the single biggest saving. |
63	| **Recurring renewals** (`worker/product-renewals.ts` + `lib/product-billing.ts`) | The generic warn→expire→grace→enforce policy already renews email subs + volumes. Add NxCloud as another product family; get dunning, grace, notifications for free. Mirrors `worker/billing.ts`. |
64	| **Customer portal shell** (`app/dashboard/*`, layout.tsx) | New `app/dashboard/nxcloud/` tab beside `servers/`, `hosting/`, `volumes/`. Same server-action + revalidatePath pattern as `lib/actions-hosting.ts`. |
65	| **SSL sweep** (`worker/ssl.ts` `sslSweep`) | Two options: let Nextcloud AIO handle its own Let's Encrypt (simplest — it's built for exactly this), OR terminate at a host reverse proxy and reuse our SSL sweep. Recommend AIO self-managed TLS for MVP. |
66	| **Backups** (`worker/backup-schedule.ts`, `platform-backups.ts`, Proxmox vzdump) | Reuse VM-level snapshot backups (the `autoBackup`/`backupIntervalHours` machinery bridged at point-of-sale in `lib/order.ts`). Nextcloud AIO *also* has borgbackup built in — offer both: platform VM snapshot + optional in-app backup. |
67	| **Metrics/monitoring** (`worker/monitor.ts`, `server-metrics.ts`) | Per-VM disk/CPU/RAM sampling already exists; the storage-usage meter customers care about comes free. |
68	| **Domains/DNS** (`lib/actions-domains-dns.ts`, Cloudflare integration) | Offer a free `<name>.nxcloud.nxeon.cloud` subdomain (wildcard A → reverse proxy or per-VM IP) and let customers point a custom domain, reusing the DNS point-to UX from hosting. |
69	| **Abuse/quotas** (`worker/abuse.ts`, `lib/net-guard.ts`, bandwidth) | Existing bandwidth accounting + abuse sweep apply to the VM unchanged. |
70	| **Terminal/SFTP** (`terminal-server/`, `lib/sftp.ts`) | Power users get console/SFTP into their instance exactly like a VPS. |
71	
72	**Net:** the only genuinely new code is (1) a Nextcloud bootstrap/install worker step, (2) a `NxCloudInstance` model + a dashboard tab, (3) plan seed data. Everything transactional/financial is reuse.
73	
74	---
75	
76	## 3. Plan tiers + pricing
77	
78	Positioning: **not a storage price war** (per-instance VMs can't beat pCloud's shared-storage $/GB). Sell **"your own private cloud, fully managed, custom domain, no per-user tax."** Competitor anchors (mid-2026): Dropbox 2 TB = $9.99/mo; pCloud 500 GB = $4.99/mo, 2 TB ~ $9.99/mo, lifetime options; Nextcloud-hosted SaaS = $6.25–$18/user/mo; self-host = free software + your VM.
79	
80	Suggested launch tiers (monthly; storage = VM disk; all include managed Nextcloud, TLS, a free subdomain, custom-domain support, unlimited "users within your instance"):
81	
82	| Tier | Storage | RAM | vCPU | Suggested price/mo | Notes |
83	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
84	| **Personal** | 100 GB | 2 GB | 1 | **$5.99** | Undercuts Dropbox's 2 TB on convenience/privacy, not raw GB. Anchor tier. |
85	| **Family / Pro** | 500 GB | 2–4 GB | 2 | **$11.99** | Matches pCloud 500 GB territory but you own the box + unlimited seats. |
86	| **Team** | 1 TB | 4 GB | 2 | **$19.99** | vs Dropbox 2 TB single-seat — here it's unlimited internal users. |
87	| **Business** | 2 TB | 8 GB | 4 | **$34.99** | Collabora/Office + Talk enabled; priority. |
88	| **Storage add-on** | +250 GB blocks | — | — | **+$3–4/mo per 250 GB** | Reuse `lib/extra-disk.ts` / volumes billing — permanent one-way growth already modelled. |
89	
90	Levers:
91	- **Annual + lifetime**: pCloud's differentiator is lifetime plans. A "2-year prepaid, 3rd year free" via the existing term/coupon machinery (`lib/billing-terms.ts`, coupon `maxTermMonths`) is low-effort and competitive.
92	- **Bandwidth**: Nextcloud sync is bandwidth-heavy. Reuse existing bandwidth accounting; set generous soft caps (e.g. 1–2 TB/mo egress) and lean on the abuse sweep for outliers.
93	- **Margin reality**: a 2 GB VM costs roughly what the Personal tier charges, so margin is thin at the bottom and improves with storage add-ons (near-pure margin on disk). Keep the entry tier as an acquisition/loss-leader; make money on storage add-ons and upsell to Team/Business.
94	
95	---
96	
97	## 4. Customer-facing features — free with Nextcloud vs build
98	
99	| Feature | Nextcloud gives free | We build |
100	|---|---|---|
101	| Web file manager (upload/download/preview/photos) | ✅ Full | — |
102	| Desktop sync client (Win/mac/Linux) | ✅ Official clients | Just document the connect URL in our panel |
103	| Mobile apps (iOS/Android) | ✅ Official apps | — |
104	| Share links (password, expiry, upload-only) | ✅ | — |

229	## 6. Security considerations
230	
231	1. **Per-tenant isolation = the whole reason to choose Approach A.** VM boundary means a Nextcloud vuln, a runaway plugin, or a compromised customer stays in that customer's VM. This is the direct lesson from the shared-hosting audit: the app-level `isHostnameClaimed` invariant and per-user FPM jails were subtle and *still* had HIGH-severity gaps. Don't re-enter that trust model for the flagship.
232	2. **Guard the multi-tenant tier the same way shared hosting is guarded.** If/when Approach B ships, keep the provisioner inert behind an `ENABLE_NXCLOUD_SHARED` flag until it's had a dedicated security review + staging validation — exactly the `ENABLE_SHARED_HOSTING` discipline in `worker/hosting.ts`.
233	3. **Encryption:** offer Nextcloud server-side encryption (at rest) on all tiers and client-side E2EE as an opt-in. Full-disk encryption of the VM's data volume is a further upsell. Be honest in marketing: managed ≠ zero-knowledge unless E2EE is on (we hold the admin creds).
234	4. **Admin credential handling:** the bootstrap admin password must follow the existing one-time-reveal-then-clear pattern (`encryptSecret` + result cleared on read). Impersonating admins must NOT be able to exfiltrate it — reuse the `assertNotImpersonating()` guards that `lib/actions-hosting.ts` already applies to SFTP-password reveal and WordPress task results.
235	5. **Abuse:** file hosting attracts piracy/malware/CSAM hosting and phishing-file distribution. Reuse the abuse sweep + bandwidth caps; add an AUP + a takedown/suspend path (the `SUSPEND` task + `adminSuspend*` pattern already exists). Consider outbound share-link rate limits. This is a real operational cost — factor it into go/no-go.
236	6. **Backups & data-loss liability:** customers will trust this with their only copy of data. VM snapshot backups must be on by default for NxCloud (bridge at point-of-sale like `lib/order.ts` does for `autoBackup`), plus Nextcloud's own borgbackup. Document retention clearly.
237	7. **Updates/patching:** Nextcloud ships security releases frequently. Lean on AIO's auto-updater; add an `UPDATE` task + a monitoring check for instances that fall behind. Unpatched customer Nextclouds are a reputational (if not blast-radius) risk.
238	8. **DNS/TLS:** custom-domain flow must validate domain ownership before issuing certs (reuse hosting's serve-verification health sweep pattern) to avoid becoming an open cert/redirect abuse vector.

Committed and pushed to `origin/feature/nxcloud`. Here is the factual report.

## NxCloud MVP — delivered

Built end-to-end in `/opt/nxeon-wt-nxcloud` (branch `feature/nxcloud`, commit `e7c76e0`). Nothing outside that worktree was touched. I did **not** run `npm run build`, `prisma generate`, or `db push` — staging is the gate. **Not tested.**

### Architecture decision (the key one)
NxCloud instances are **backed by a real `Server`** created through the existing PROVISION path. The backing VM references a **hidden `Plan`** (`active:false`, slug `nxcloud-<tier>`) whose `priceCents` **equals the tier's display price**. Consequence: **renewals, dunning, grace, suspend and terminate are 100% inherited from the audited VPS billing sweep** (`worker/billing.ts`, which bills the plan's full price with no promo) — there is **no NxCloud-specific money code**, so no double-billing risk. `NxCloudInstance` is the product wrapper (subdomain, one-time admin creds, app status). This is the spec's "reuse `Server` + a plan flag" §5, and it's why the build is small.

### Files created
- `prisma/seed-nxcloud.ts` — seeds the `nextcloud` OsTemplate + 4 tiers (each: hidden backing `Plan` + `NxCloudPlan`, priced in lockstep)
- `lib/nxcloud.ts` — pure helpers (subdomain validation, FQDN/URL)
- `lib/actions-nxcloud.ts` — `orderNxCloud`, `listNxcloudInstances`, `revealNxcloudAdminPassword`, `resetNxcloudAdminPassword`, `terminateNxcloud`, `adminListNxcloud`
- `worker/nxcloud.ts` — install-script builder, provision hook, `nxcloudProvisionSweep`, `nxcloudTaskSweep`
- `app/(marketing)/nxcloud/page.tsx` — marketing page (navy/violet/cyan design system, hero/features/steps/plans/FAQ/CTA)
- `app/dashboard/nxcloud/page.tsx` + `components/customer/NxcloudClient.tsx` — customer tab
- `app/admin/nxcloud/page.tsx` — admin fleet visibility (plans + instance table)

### Files edited
- `prisma/schema.prisma` — new models/enums + back-relations on `User`, `Server`, `Plan`
- `worker/index.ts` — import + provision hook (`__nxcloudSetup`) + cloud-init consumption + sweep registration (~30s cadence) + `lastNxcloudSweep`
- `app/dashboard/layout.tsx` (nav item), `lib/admin-groups.ts` + `lib/rbac.ts` (admin route → `fleet`), `components/marketing/MarketingHeader.tsx` (products menu), `lib/settings.ts` (`nxcloud_zone` default), `app/dashboard/servers/page.tsx` (hide NxCloud-backed VMs from the raw VPS list)

### Exact schema additions
- **`enum NxCloudStatus`** { PENDING, PROVISIONING, ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, FAILED, DELETING }
- **`enum NxCloudTaskKind`** { RESET_ADMIN_PW, ENABLE_APP, UPDATE }
- **`NxCloudPlan`**: id, slug@unique, name, priceCents, storageGB, ramMB, vcpu, bandwidthTB, collabora, talk, featured, tagline, active, sortOrder, createdAt, **serverPlanId→Plan**, instances[]
- **`NxCloudInstance`**: id, userId→User(Cascade), planId→NxCloudPlan, **serverId?@unique→Server(SetNull)**, subdomain@unique, customDomain?@unique, sslActive, status, adminUser, **adminPassEnc?** (encrypted), storageUsedMB?, storageQuotaMB, usageAt?, version?, error?, provisionedAt?, timestamps, tasks[]; @@index userId, status
- **`NxCloudTask`**: id, instanceId→NxCloudInstance(Cascade), kind, **status HostingTaskStatus** (reused enum), payload?, result? (one-time secret), error?, timestamps
- Back-relations: `User.nxcloudInstances`, `Server.nxcloudInstance`, `Plan.nxcloudPlans`

### Seed / setting needed
- Run `npx tsx prisma/seed-nxcloud.ts` (after `db push`) — creates the `nextcloud` image + Personal $5.99/100GB, Family $11.99/500GB, Team $19.99/1TB, Business $34.99/2TB (Collabora+Talk).
- `nxcloud_zone` setting (default `nxcloud.nxeon.cloud`).

### Provisioning steps the worker runs
1. `orderNxCloud` creates the `Server` + `NxCloudInstance(PENDING)` + PROVISION job atomically after the wallet charge.
2. `provision()` clones/resizes/boots the VM as usual; the `nxcloudSetupForServer` hook (before cloud-init) generates the **one-time admin password** (encrypted, once), flips the instance to PROVISIONING, and returns an **idempotent Docker + Nextcloud (official image) + MariaDB + Redis + Caddy** install script (admin creds + trusted domain injected; Caddy auto-TLS). It's appended to the existing cloud-init `runcmd`.
3. `nxcloudProvisionSweep` probes `https://<fqdn>/status.php`; on `installed:true` → **ACTIVE** (+ version, sslActive), else keeps waiting and after a 30-min grace flips to **ACTIVE-with-caveat** + admin alert (the COMPLETED_WITH_ISSUES analog). It also mirrors a suspended backing VM onto the instance. SANDBOX simulates a completed install.

Order charges `NxCloudPlan.priceCents` (full, **no first-month-free**) via `debitWallet` inside the same tx that writes the wallet line, a PAID invoice, the Server, the instance, and the job — a rolled-back charge leaves nothing. `Server.termPromoPercent=0` (sold at full → no phantom proration credit). Renewals bill the same price through the audited VPS sweep. displayed === charged === renewed.
